llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: it watches conversations, detects behavioral patterns, runs simulated hearings via the agent's LLM, and writes results to ~/.openclaw/courtroom/. Before installing or enabling it: 1) Review the code (skill.js) yourself or with someone you trust — the skill persists conversation evidence locally. 2) Consider privacy: verdict and eval files may contain user/assistant message text; decide whether that’s acceptable and where files will be stored/retained. 3) If you don’t want continuous monitoring, keep autonomy disabled or only invoke the skill manually. 4) Check file permissions on ~/.openclaw/courtroom and implement retention/cleanup if necessary. 5) If you expect networking or external integrations, audit for hidden endpoints (none were found in these files). If any of these points concern you or you need tighter controls, disable autonomous invocation and audit or sandbox the skill before use.
llm.findings: [prompt-injection:ignore-previous-instructions] expected: SKILL.md and skill.js explicitly list common jailbreak/prompt-injection phrases (e.g., 'ignore previous instructions') as things to detect. The pre-scan flagged the phrase, but its inclusion appears to be part of detection logic rather than an attempt to perform prompt-injection against the host.
